title: Article 311 — Dismissal, removal or reduction in rank of persons employed in civil capacities under the Union or a State

content.overview: Article 311 protects civil servants: no person who is a member of a civil service of the Union or an all-India service or a civil service of a State or holds a civil post under the Union or a State shall be dismissed or removed by an authority subordinate to that by which he was appointed. No such person shall be dismissed, removed or reduced in rank except after an inquiry in which he has been informed of the charges and given a reasonable opportunity of being heard in respect of those charges. Exceptions apply where a person is dismissed/removed/reduced on the ground of conduct leading to conviction on a criminal charge; or where the authority is satisfied that for some reason to be recorded it is not reasonably practicable to hold such inquiry; or where the President or Governor is satisfied that in the interest of the security of the State it is not expedient to hold such inquiry.
content.glance: Civil servant: no dismissal/removal by subordinate authority; no dismissal/removal/reduction in rank without inquiry and reasonable opportunity of hearing — subject to conviction, impracticability, or security-of-State exceptions.
content.study:
Article 311 is the core constitutional safeguard for civil servants:
(1) No dismissal or removal by an authority subordinate to the appointing authority.
(2) No dismissal, removal or reduction in rank except after inquiry with information of charges and reasonable opportunity of being heard — except: (a) conduct leading to conviction on a criminal charge; (b) authority records that it is not reasonably practicable to hold the inquiry; (c) President/Governor satisfied that in the interest of the security of the State it is not expedient to hold the inquiry.

Examination: appointing-authority rule; inquiry + hearing; three exceptions; distinction between punishment and non-punitive termination/retirement.

sections.heading: Safeguards and exceptions
sections.body:
1. No dismissal/removal by authority subordinate to the appointing authority.
2. Inquiry + reasonable opportunity of hearing before dismissal, removal or reduction in rank.
3. Exceptions: (a) conviction on criminal charge; (b) inquiry not reasonably practicable (reasons recorded); (c) security of the State (President/Governor satisfaction).

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the safeguards under Article 311.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 311 provides that no civil servant of the Union or a State (including members of all-India services and holders of civil posts) shall be dismissed or removed by an authority subordinate to that by which he was appointed. No such person shall be dismissed, removed or reduced in rank except after an inquiry in which he has been informed of the charges against him and given a reasonable opportunity of being heard in respect of those charges. These inquiry requirements do not apply where the person is dismissed, removed or reduced in rank on the ground of conduct which has led to his conviction on a criminal charge; or where the competent authority records that it is not reasonably practicable to hold such inquiry; or where the President or Governor is satisfied that in the interest of the security of the State it is not expedient to hold such inquiry.

examTips: Appointing-authority rule; inquiry + hearing; three exceptions (conviction, impracticable, security).

keyTakeaways: Art 311: dismissal/removal/reduction safeguards for civil servants.
